edit.description: `harness()` is the last place that can still see whether the author passed a `contract` at all — `init.contract ?? rootDefaultContract` erases the distinction the moment it composes. Record that declaredness on the composed harness so the row writer can read it; the defaulting itself is unchanged.

`assemblyFactRows` writes the marker: one `contract` fact per `expect`-bound kind, naming the kind in the row's `from` column beside the `edge` facts' own use of it, and one `contract` fact carrying no kind for an authored root contract — the same kind-absent-means-root discriminator `compileDeclarations` already writes for a root clause row.

`AssemblyFactRow`'s fact discriminator widens from `mode | edge` to include `contract` (the doc comment on `fact` states the set). The marker rides the row's existing columns, so no column is added — but the widened doc comment does re-bless `sdk/src/generated/AssemblyFactRow.ts` under `BLESS_SEAM_BINDINGS=1`, which `BUILD_SURFACE_PATHS` already allows every scoped tick, so that path is deliberately not listed here.

Both rows-or-default branches read the marker, which means both take the assembly slice their callers never passed: `builtin_contract` (src/compose.rs:1566) gains an `assembly` argument beside its `clauses`/`kinds`/`kind`, and `root_contract` (src/compose.rs:258) gains one beside its `clauses`. Declared = the marker OR any row of that owner's, so an older lock carrying rows keeps its contract and one carrying neither still falls to the embedded default — decision 0024's read-time normalization, which is what makes the upgrade lossless.
Signature ripple, one call site: `builtin_contract` at src/read.rs:2410, inside the per-kind contract loop. `declarations` is already in scope, so the edit is the one added assembly argument.

Signature ripple, two call sites: `builtin_contract` at src/gate.rs:246 (under `with_joined_clauses`) and `root_contract` at src/gate.rs:519. `declarations` is in scope at both. Riding this file's opening: the coverage-note comment at src/gate.rs:733 still describes the call below it as naming "known Claude Code surfaces present on disk that no kind governs", a class 1f8bef99 retired — re-point it at the two classes `coverage_note::check` actually emits, `coverage.checked` and `coverage.unclaimed-entry`.
Signature ripple, three call sites: `builtin_contract` at src/main.rs:619 and src/main.rs:668, `root_contract` at src/main.rs:775 (inside `guarded_loci`). `declarations` is in scope at all three.
Signature ripple, one call site: `root_contract` at src/install.rs:1149, where the composed root's clauses are searched by predicate. `declarations` is the enclosing function's own parameter.

Regenerate: the memberless built-in program binds every kind through `expect`, so the embedded lock gains one `contract` fact per built-in kind (sixteen). Its root contract is undeclared (the program names none) and gains no fact. Regeneration is a re-run of `@dtmd/temper/claude-code`'s own emit re-embedded verbatim per the file's header, never a hand-added row.

The other derived lock in the tree, regenerated the same way rather than hand-edited: it gains one `contract` marker per `expect`-bound kind of the example program (eight). Regenerate with `ln -sfn $PWD/sdk examples/base-harness/.temper/node_modules/@dtmd/temper` (the link is gitignored) then `cargo run -- emit --into examples/base-harness/.temper`.

The gate that forces the example regeneration above, and the one real consumer in this entry's ripple: `emit_program_runs_the_shipped_example_harness` (tests/it/emit.rs:2432) copies `examples/base-harness/` to a scratch tree, re-emits it, and byte-compares the derived `lock.toml` against the committed one — so an inexact regeneration fails here, not in `builtin_lock_frozen.rs`. Expected to need no edit; listed so a re-pin lands inside the fence. The file's own `AssemblyFactRow {…}` literal (tests/it/emit.rs:239) is exhaustive and keeps compiling — the marker adds no column.
The byte-compare that forces the regeneration above. Expected to need no edit — listed so a shift in the assembly family's row order can be re-pinned here rather than outside the entry's fence.
The `contract` fact round-trips through the lock reader and writer; `expect(kind, [])` composes an empty contract for that kind, while a kind the lock marks nothing for keeps its embedded floor.
A root `contract: []` composes a root contract with no clauses, where today it composes the shipped three; a lock with neither marker nor root rows still composes `rootDefaultContract`.
The emitted declaration rows carry the marker for an authored contract — empty or not, per kind and at the root — and omit it where the author declared none.

summary: An authored empty clause array is a declared contract: the lock marks declaredness per kind and at the root, and a default applies only where nothing is declared.

tests.asserts: an authored empty root contract composes no root clauses, and a lock carrying neither the marker nor a root row still composes the shipped root default
the `contract` assembly fact round-trips, `expect(kind, [])` composes an empty contract for that kind, and an unmarked rowless kind keeps its embedded floor
emit writes the declared-contract marker per `expect`-bound kind and for an authored root contract, and omits it for an undeclared root
the embedded lock still byte-equals @dtmd/temper/claude-code's memberless emit after the regeneration
the shipped example harness still re-emits to its committed lock byte-for-byte once the eight `contract` markers land in it
the gauntlet's projection-tree snapshot re-blesses with the fixture's one added `contract` marker row (`cargo insta accept`; snapshots are fence-allowed)

acceptance: `cargo test` and `pnpm --dir sdk test` green: `expect(kind, [])` and a root `contract: []` each compose a contract with no clauses, a lock carrying neither marker nor rows still composes the embedded default, and both derived locks byte-equal their regenerated emit.
notes: 0072 rules the collision between builtins.md's "never a privileged form" and the code: both branches key on row presence, so an authored `[]` reads as silence. The marker rides `AssemblyFactRow`'s existing columns — a new `KindFactRow` column is a required field at 133 literal sites. A prior build reached all five gates green with six paths outside the fence; the example lock's byte-compare is the last ripple path, folded this tick. scoped at dca24238
